name: Paid holiday by law, from the labour codes cited

measures.definition: Statutory paid annual leave for a full-time employee on a five-day week, at the baseline service level in each note. Calendar-day entitlements use the explicit five-day-week equivalent in the observation, not an exact individual workday entitlement.

coverage.geography: the 26 countries with a tax model

rights.attribution: Borgo contributors, from the labour codes cited in each figure's note

vetted.notes: Official statutes and labour-authority guidance, with an official source linked on every figure and country-by-country verification in docs/pension-leave-audit.md.

caveats: Baseline entitlements only: service, accrual, age, working pattern, sector and collective agreements can change the applicable leave. Hungary, Norway and Switzerland have modelled age adjustments; service progression is described but not calculated.
The UK entitlement is 28 days including any bank holidays the employer counts towards it; public holidays are not an additional guaranteed paid entitlement there.
Spain and the UAE grant 30 calendar days, represented as 30 × 5/7 equivalent working days. The actual number of working days depends on leave dates; UAE public holidays within leave count towards it.
Canada uses the federal baseline, not a uniform rule for all provincial employees. First-year accrual and qualifying service differ by country.
